source_metadata.etymology_text: From Middle Dutch sommich, summich, zomich, somich, from som (“any, some”) + -ich. Cognate with Middle Low German sōmich, sommich, summich, Old Frisian sumich (whence West Frisian sommige).

From Middle Dutch sommich, somich, from som (“any, some”) + -ich. The simplex som derives from Old Dutch sum (“any, some”), from Proto-West Germanic *sum (“some”). It is found also in other combinations such as soms and somtijds.
Related to English some.
From Middle Dutch na, from Old Dutch *nāh, *nā, from Proto-West Germanic *nāhw, from Proto-Germanic *nēhwaz.
From Middle Dutch naest, from Old Dutch *nāist, *nāst, from Proto-Germanic *nēhwist (“nearest, closest”).
From Middle Dutch naest, from Old Dutch *nāist, *nāst, from Proto-Germanic *nēhwist (“nearest, closest”).
From Middle Dutch naesten, from naest (“closest, next”) (modern Dutch naast).
